title: Gain-boosted cascode OTA
description: A cascode OTA whose cascode devices are regulated by auxiliary 'booster' amplifiers (gain-boosting / regulated cascode). A booster senses the cascoded device's drain and drives the cascode gate to hold its source fixed, so the local feedback multiplies the cascode's own intrinsic gain by the booster gain: each side's output resistance becomes about $A_{v0,boost} * A_{v0,casc} * r_o$. That lifts the single-stage gain by the booster gain — often 20-40 dB — without adding a stack device or a second signal-path pole. The price is the booster's own bandwidth: it forms a pole-zero doublet that slows settling, so the closed-loop settling is estimate-grade and the sim owns sign-off. The stack is parameterized by its NODES: the tail node is pinned so the produced $CM_{in}$ equals $CM_{dc}$, and the internal nodes $V_a$ (input drain) and $V_b$ (mirror drain) are choice params — every device $V_{DS}$ is a subtraction between adjacent nodes, every source-above-bulk device carries its true body bias, and the drops sum to the rail by construction. Here one booster child models the regulation gain and is applied to both the NMOS and PMOS output cascodes.

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget; the gamma-model total lands near 19 nV/rtHz at the default currents. the budget carries about 30% headroom over the gamma-model row (no measured floor exists for this topology)

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low edge — proven exactly by the cm-lo edge at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.85-1.18 V on sky130 tt at the shipped choices). The edge proves the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high edge — its ENDPOINT proven by the cm-hi edge the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis. The slider stops where the stack does: with V_a holding the pair's drain low, the tail node cannot climb past the bracket and the topology genuinely cannot take a higher CM — the telescopic's known input-range ceiling

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; the NMOS nodes climb to it and the PMOS nodes descend to it

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the pair's source. Solved rather than set: bisected between min and max (the BRACKET) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. The max must stay far enough below V_a for the pair to size at the top end — the input-sat guardrail owns saturation; the bracket only has to keep both ends on the table

params.name: V_a
params.note: the NMOS-side internal node: input drain and NMOS-cascode source. The input vds is V_a - V_tail and the cascode's is V_out_dc - V_a, by construction

params.name: V_b
params.note: the PMOS-side internal node: mirror drain and PMOS-cascode source. The mirror vds is VDD - V_b and the cascode's is V_b - V_out_dc, by construction

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

params.name: I_boost
params.note: booster tail current; sets the booster bandwidth (settling doublet) — spend enough to keep it faster than the main loop

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current and the input-referred noise

params.name: gm_id_casc
params.note: cascode-device inversion: sets the un-boosted cascode gain av0_casc

params.name: gm_id_mir
params.note: load-mirror inversion: lower gm/ID gives higher mirror ro

params.name: gm_id_bo
params.note: booster-device inversion: sets the booster gain that multiplies each cascode's ro

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current; its ro is boosted by the NMOS cascode and its booster.

doc.title: NMOS output cascode
doc.description: Regulated cascode over the input device; its intrinsic gain av0, times the booster gain, sets the NMOS-side Rout.

doc.title: PMOS output cascode
doc.description: Regulated cascode over the load mirror; its intrinsic gain av0, times the booster gain, sets the PMOS-side Rout.

doc.title: Load mirror device
doc.description: PMOS load-mirror side at half the tail current; its ro, cascoded and boosted, sets the PMOS-side output resistance.

doc.title: Gain-boost amplifier
doc.description: The regulating auxiliary amp, modelled as a single gain stage; its DC gain av0 multiplies each cascode's intrinsic gain, and its own ft (gm/2*pi*cgg) sets the settling doublet.

rows.name: CM_in
rows.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed bisection

rows.name: Rout_n
rows.note: NMOS side: input ro boosted by the cascode gain and again by the booster gain

rows.name: Rout_p
rows.note: PMOS side: mirror ro boosted by the cascode gain and again by the booster gain

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the two regulated-cascode sides in parallel

rows.name: f_boost
rows.note: estimate: the booster's own ft, a proxy for its bandwidth; the doublet near this frequency governs settling

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input pair plus the load mirror's own density referred by gm_mir/gm_in; the boosters sit outside the main signal path and add little

rows.name: vos
rows.expr: sqrt(pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, gm_id_in)^2 + (pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, mir__W, L_mir, gm_id_mir)*mir__gm/in__gm)^2)
rows.note: input-pair offset plus the load-mirror offset referred by the gm ratio

rules.note: estimate: the booster must be faster than the main loop or its doublet slows settling; sim owns the real settling
node placement: V_a must sit at least a vdsat above the tail node — the drops sum to the rail by construction, so what is left to check is that each node leaves its device saturated
node placement: the output DC must sit at least a vdsat above V_a
node placement: V_b must sit at least a vdsat above the output DC
node placement: V_b must leave the mirror at least a vdsat below VDD
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below; the cm-lo/cm-hi edges prove the range ENDS close, and the CM_dc sweep shows the whole landscape

edges.name: cm-lo
edges.note: the claimed low edge, proven exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo — its own tail-node solve from the full bracket, its own devices — and every hard rule must hold there

edges.name: cm-hi
edges.note: the claimed high edge, proven the same way. Edges prove the ENDPOINTS; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
